subject.title: [Feature]: Surface delivery correlation data on message_sent hooks

question: Should `message_sent` expose queue identity only when a durable queued delivery exists, or should OpenClaw mint a logical delivery ID and attempt number for every outbound dispatch?
rationale: Both choices are implementable, but they create different permanent Plugin SDK semantics for direct sends, retries, recovery, and idempotency; repository behavior does not currently establish one as the public contract.

options.title: Queue-scoped identity
options.body: Expose a hook-safe receipt and available run correlation now, with optional `deliveryId` and clearly defined `attemptNumber` only for durable queued deliveries.

options.title: Universal delivery identity
options.body: Mint and propagate a logical identity for every outbound dispatch, accepting the broader delivery-lifecycle and persistence design work.

options.title: Receipt first
options.body: Expose the receipt and available run correlation now while deferring all queue identity fields to a separate lifecycle API design.

recommendation.title: Queue-scoped identity
recommendation.body: Expose a hook-safe receipt and available run correlation now, with optional `deliveryId` and clearly defined `attemptNumber` only for durable queued deliveries.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior outbound `message:sent` correlation work is the strongest available feature-history signal for this API choice.
